item.title: Part-time Pensacola officer admits to decade-long pill buying scheme, FDLE says
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A part-time Pensacola Police Department officer has admitted to purchasing between 50 and 60 pills per week while wearing his police uniform over a 10-year period, according to a statement he provided to the Florida Department of Law Enforcement. The officer was arrested on charges related to buying narcotics in uniform. The admission to FDLE…
item.content:encoded:
A part-time Pensacola Police Department officer has admitted to purchasing between 50 and 60 pills per week while wearing his police uniform over a 10-year period, according to a statement he provided to the Florida Department of Law Enforcement.

The officer was arrested on charges related to buying narcotics in uniform. The admission to FDLE investigators reveals the scope of the alleged illegal drug purchases, which authorities say spanned a decade.

Details about the officer's identity, the specific charges he faces, and the circumstances that led to the FDLE investigation have not yet been fully disclosed. The Pensacola Police Department has not released an official statement regarding the arrest or the officer's employment status.

item.title: Escambia County extends emergency declaration; residents push for faster debris removal after Hurricane Issa
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County commissioners have extended the local emergency declaration as the region continues recovery operations following Hurricane Issa, according to reporting from Citizen Portal News Florida. The extension keeps disaster protocols in place as cleanup and restoration efforts move forward across the county. Emergency declarations allow…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County commissioners have extended the local emergency declaration as the region continues recovery operations following Hurricane Issa, according to reporting from Citizen Portal News Florida.

The extension keeps disaster protocols in place as cleanup and restoration efforts move forward across the county. Emergency declarations allow local governments to mobilize resources, expedite spending, and coordinate mutual aid more efficiently during recovery phases.

However, residents have grown impatient with the pace of debris removal—a critical bottleneck in post-hurricane recovery. Homeowners and business owners are calling for the county to accelerate collection and hauling operations to clear streets and properties more quickly. Debris management after major hurricanes is typically one of the longest and most resource-intensive phases of disaster recovery, often competing with other urgent restoration needs for equipment and personnel.

item.content:encoded:
The Pensacola Ice Flyers' season got off to a rough start Saturday night, dropping their Opening Night matchup 4-2 to the Macon Mayhem in front of 5,994 fans at The Hangar.

The Ice Flyers came out strong defensively in the first period, outshooting Macon 13-7, but couldn't find the back of the net. The Mayhem's Mason Hoehn broke through early in the second period to give Macon the lead, and despite a Pensacola push later in the frame, the visitors held on for the win.

The loss marks an inauspicious start to the season for the local professional hockey team, which will look to bounce back in upcoming matchups.

item.content:encoded:
North Escambia is in for a stretch of crisp fall weather through early this week, with abundant sunshine and clear skies dominating the forecast. Northeast winds will keep conditions breezy, holding daytime highs in the upper 60s to lower 70s through Monday.

Temperatures will begin climbing midweek as a warming trend moves in. Expect highs to reach the mid-70s by Tuesday, then push into the upper 70s as the week progresses. The combination of cool mornings and gradually warming afternoons will make for classic fall conditions ideal for outdoor activity.

Ron DeSantis on Friday in Milton to highlight ongoing recovery efforts following recent storm damage across the Panhandle, according to North Escambia reporting. Salzman praised state agencies for what she described as unprecedented emergency response times in the wake of the storm. The…
item.content:encoded:
Florida State Rep. Michelle Salzman joined Gov. Ron DeSantis on Friday in Milton to highlight ongoing recovery efforts following recent storm damage across the Panhandle, according to North Escambia reporting.

Salzman praised state agencies for what she described as unprecedented emergency response times in the wake of the storm. The representative emphasized that residents in affected areas—including parts of Escambia and Santa Rosa counties—should not hesitate to reach out for state assistance if they've suffered damage or losses.

"We hear you," Salzman said at the news conference, signaling the state's commitment to supporting communities still working through recovery. The joint appearance with DeSantis underscored coordination between state leadership and local representatives on resource deployment and aid distribution across the hardest-hit areas of Northwest Florida.

item.content:encoded:
Conditions are roughening up in the waters off Pensacola, with the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration's buoy 42039 reporting significant wave heights of 7.2 feet Sunday afternoon, according to Florida Gulf Signal.

The marine weather station, positioned in the Gulf near Pensacola, is also recording northerly winds at 21.4 knots and air temperatures around 74 degrees. Waves are building at intervals of about 7 seconds.

Those conditions suggest choppy water for boaters and beachgoers. If you're planning to head out on the water today or tonight, check current conditions and heed any marine warnings before you go.

item.title: Valparaiso Post Office Closes Due to Structural Damage; Services Move to Niceville
item.dc:creator: newsroom

Customers can now access postal services at the Niceville Main Post Office, 90 Palm Boulevard North, which is handling P.O. Box…
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. Postal Service has temporarily suspended retail operations at the Valparaiso Post Office on Edge Avenue effective immediately due to structural damage to the building, according to a USPS announcement Saturday.

Customers can now access postal services at the Niceville Main Post Office, 90 Palm Boulevard North, which is handling P.O. Box services and retail operations including stamp purchases, mailing, and package shipping. The Niceville location operates Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:45 p.m., and Saturdays from 9 a.m. to noon. Sunday service is not available.

The USPS said it prioritizes the safety of customers and employees and will provide updates as work progresses to reopen the Valparaiso facility. Residents are asked to bring proper photo identification when picking up mail and packages at the temporary location.

item.title: AAA warns drivers: Over a third ignore 'Move Over' law near roadside vehicles
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Today marks National Slow Down, Move Over Day, and AAA is sounding the alarm about a troubling disconnect between what drivers say they do and what they actually do when approaching disabled vehicles on the roadside. A new AAA Foundation for Traffic Safety survey found that over 90% of Florida drivers claim they slow down or move over when passing…
item.content:encoded:
Today marks National Slow Down, Move Over Day, and AAA is sounding the alarm about a troubling disconnect between what drivers say they do and what they actually do when approaching disabled vehicles on the roadside.

A new AAA Foundation for Traffic Safety survey found that over 90% of Florida drivers claim they slow down or move over when passing a disabled vehicle, tow truck, or police car on the shoulder. But observational research tells a different story: only 64% of drivers actually change lanes or reduce speed. More than one-third do neither. "Drivers often think roadside danger only affects police officers, firefighters, and tow truck operators," said Mark Jenkins, AAA spokesman for The Auto Club Group. "But anyone can become vulnerable at the roadside. A flat tire, dead battery, or mechanical problem can place drivers and passengers just feet from moving traffic."

The stakes are serious. Between 2019 and 2023, more than 2,100 people were struck and killed while stranded or working at the roadside. In 2025 alone, 15 roadside service providers died in Move Over-related incidents, several involving impaired or hit-and-run drivers. A separate survey found that 56% of Floridians listed being struck by another vehicle as their top concern if their own car broke down.

Under Florida law, drivers must move over for all stopped vehicles displaying flashing or hazard lights—law enforcement, EMS, fire, construction, and disabled vehicles. If changing lanes isn't safe, motorists must reduce speed and proceed with caution. All 50 states have similar laws, though specific requirements vary.

item.content:encoded:
A wind advisory remains in effect across portions of the Florida Panhandle including the North Escambia area, with strong gusts expected to create an enhanced threat for downed trees and power outages through the weekend.

Saturday will be sunny with a high near 69 degrees, but the gusty winds are expected to persist. The combination of dry conditions and strong winds has also elevated wildfire risk across the region on Saturday, according to the forecast.

Residents should secure loose outdoor items and be prepared for potential power disruptions. Motorists should exercise caution, particularly on bridges and in open areas where wind gusts can be strongest.

item.title: DeSantis Details Storm Recovery Push for Panhandle, Eyes Federal Aid
item.dc:creator: newsroom

According to reporting on the event, DeSantis discussed the distribution of emergency resources to affected areas, an expedited request for federal disaster…
item.content:encoded:
Governor Ron DeSantis highlighted ongoing relief efforts across the Florida Panhandle during a press conference in Milton, outlining a coordinated state response to storm damage in the region.

According to reporting on the event, DeSantis discussed the distribution of emergency resources to affected areas, an expedited request for federal disaster declaration status, and a new state partnership that will deploy travel trailers to help displaced homeowners rebuild. The governor's visit underscores the scale of recovery work facing inland communities throughout the Panhandle following recent severe weather.

The relief push combines state resources with federal coordination, aiming to accelerate assistance for residents dealing with property damage and displacement across the region.

item.content:encoded:
Governor Ron DeSantis announced Friday the appointment of Stephen Beckman to the Construction Industry Licensing Board. Beckman currently serves as director of Building Services for the City of Naples and holds multiple certifications including General Contractor, Building Code Administrator, and Plans Examiner through the Florida Department of Business Regulation.

Beckman is active in professional organizations, including the Building Officials Association of Florida and the Association of State Floodplain Managers. He earned his bachelor's degree from Concordia College.

The appointment is subject to confirmation by the Florida Senate, according to the Governor's Press Office.

item.title: Milton prioritizes school bus stops for debris removal ahead of reopening
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The City of Milton is focusing storm debris removal efforts around school bus stops and campuses as Santa Rosa County schools prepare to reopen next week following Hurricane Isaias, according to a city news release issued Friday. Crew began collection operations Tuesday, October 13, and are working daily through November to clear an estimated…
item.content:encoded:
The City of Milton is focusing storm debris removal efforts around school bus stops and campuses as Santa Rosa County schools prepare to reopen next week following Hurricane Isaias, according to a city news release issued Friday.

Crew began collection operations Tuesday, October 13, and are working daily through November to clear an estimated 400,000 cubic yards of storm debris plus another 35,000 cubic yards of construction and demolition material. Residents may notice debris trucks in neighborhoods collecting some piles while leaving others — the city says crews are prioritizing school-related access first and will return for additional collection as operations progress.

Parents and guardians should keep children closely supervised near bus stops and debris work zones. The city warns of active heavy equipment, utility crews, and recovery activities in neighborhoods. The debris processing site is located about three blocks from Rhodes Elementary School at Byrom and James Streets, where motorists and pedestrians should exercise caution.

Preliminary damage assessments show about 60% of Milton structures sustained some storm damage, with roughly 5% deemed uninhabitable. The city asked residents to remain patient as recovery continues.
